sections.title: International Private Banking and Wealth Management AI
sections.description: For Citigroup Private Bank, HSBC Private Banking, and Miami's LatAm-focused wealth management community.

blocks.heading: Cross-border AML and transaction monitoring
paragraphs: ML for the AML programs of Miami's international banks serving Latin American HNW clients — the specific money laundering typologies of Latin American wealth (real estate-based placement, trade invoice manipulation, US shell company layering) require ML models trained on LatAm-specific patterns that domestic US AML models miss.

blocks.heading: Politically Exposed Person (PEP) risk monitoring
paragraphs: ML for the enhanced due diligence programs for the large number of politically exposed persons (Latin American politicians, government officials, and their families) who have Miami banking relationships — predicting which PEP relationships represent elevated corruption risk based on the home country's corruption environment and the client's transaction patterns.

blocks.heading: Multi-jurisdiction wealth structuring analytics
paragraphs: ML for the complex wealth management strategies of Latin American HNW families with assets in multiple countries — FATCA reporting obligations, CRS (Common Reporting Standard) compliance, and the cross-border tax planning analytics for clients with US, LatAm, and European asset holdings simultaneously.

sections.title: Latin America Cross-Border Payments AI
sections.description: For the payment companies serving the US-LatAm payments corridor.

blocks.heading: Real-time LatAm payment fraud detection
paragraphs: ML for the payment companies processing real-time transfers between the US and Brazil, Mexico, Colombia, Chile, and other LatAm markets — the specific fraud patterns of cross-border payments (account takeover using LatAm social engineering techniques, synthetic identity fraud exploiting US-LatAm identity verification gaps) require corridor-specific ML.

blocks.heading: Brazilian Pix and LatAm instant payment analytics
paragraphs: ML for the US payment companies integrating with Brazil's Pix instant payment system and the other LatAm instant payment schemes — predicting fraud in the instant, irrevocable payment context where traditional chargeback-based risk management doesn't apply.

blocks.heading: FX and currency risk ML
paragraphs: ML for the FX risk management of payment companies handling US-LatAm transactions through volatile LatAm currency corridors — predicting BRL, COP, CLP, and other LatAm currency rate movements for the payment companies managing FX exposure.

sections.title: Florida Insurtech and Catastrophe Analytics
sections.description: For the insurtech companies and traditional insurers addressing Florida's catastrophic weather market.

blocks.heading: Hurricane and wind risk ML
paragraphs: ML for the Florida property insurers — predicting hurricane landfall probability, track modeling, and the specific wind damage patterns of Florida's built environment for the property catastrophe underwriting that is Florida's dominant insurance AI application.

blocks.heading: Flood risk analytics
paragraphs: ML for the Florida flood insurance market — the intersection of NFIP (National Flood Insurance Program) and private flood insurance creates specific analytics demand for the private flood insurers filling the NFIP coverage gap in Florida's high-risk coastal markets.

blocks.heading: Citizens Insurance off-boarding analytics
paragraphs: ML for the private insurers taking policies from Citizens Property Insurance Corporation — the Florida Citizens depopulation program creates specific policyholder risk analytics for private insurers evaluating Citizens policy acquisition.

sections.title: Cryptocurrency and Digital Asset Analytics
sections.description: Miami has become one of the US's most crypto-friendly cities.

blocks.heading: Cryptocurrency transaction monitoring and analytics
paragraphs: ML for the crypto exchanges and digital asset companies operating in Florida — chain analytics for AML compliance, on-chain transaction monitoring for suspicious activity, and the SAR-filing analytics for the Florida-licensed money services businesses in the digital asset space.

blocks.heading: Digital asset portfolio analytics
paragraphs: ML for the family offices and wealth managers offering digital asset exposure to Miami's HNW client base — risk modeling for crypto portfolios with the specific volatility characteristics and correlation structures of digital assets.

sections.title: Florida FinTech AI regulatory context
sections.description: Key regulatory considerations for FinTech AI development in Florida.

blocks.heading: Florida Office of Financial Regulation (OFR)
paragraphs: Florida's financial services regulator oversees Miami's FinTech companies — ClickMasters designs Miami FinTech AI with Florida OFR examination readiness.

blocks.heading: Florida Digital Bill of Rights
paragraphs: Florida's privacy law creates data governance requirements for Miami FinTech consumer applications.

blocks.heading: Florida's no-income-tax financial environment
paragraphs: Florida's elimination of personal income taxes continues to attract financial services companies, fund managers, and wealth management firms from New York and Connecticut — a migration trend accelerated by COVID-19 that continues to drive Miami's FinTech growth.
